processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea, used for both green and black tea. The processing follows whichever is being made.
harvest_season: A mid-season cultivar, reaching one bud and three leaves in early April in spring.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it, green or black.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the tea made: typically light yellow-green as a green tea, red-amber as a black tea.
appearance_wet: Depends on the tea made from it.
taste_profile: No tasting record specific to this cultivar is well established; it is valued for good quality in both green and black tea.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Chinese green tea made from it; use black tea parameters if the leaf was made into black tea.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name. Its leaf goes into regional green and black teas sold by their class: green teas as the current spring harvest, black teas usually within a couple of years.
description:
Zhuyeqi is a Chinese tea cultivar, a clonal, mid-season diploid plant known from Hunan and the parent name for selections such as No. 9 and No. 12. You will meet it mostly as a line in a producer's notes.

The bush is tall with a half-open or open habit and a clear main stem at the base. It reaches one bud and three leaves in early April, and it is considered suited to the green tea areas north and south of the Yangtze.

It is used for both green and black tea, so the cup depends on the maker. There is no well-established taste profile for the cultivar alone; brew according to the tea you have in hand.

For buyers, the name says something about the plant and little about the cup. Ask what style was made and which harvest it comes from, and if you are curious, compare it with its numbered selections.
history: Little is documented in accessible form about when and where it was first selected. It is recorded under the name Camellia sinensis cv. Zhuyeqi, and it is regarded as worth planting widely for its yield, quality and hardiness.
